selection_note: The original Self-RAG PDF is retained as supplementary reading but excluded from the four-paper numeric core because its TriviaQA answer-containment accuracy is not the same as strict Exact Match. DPR was added so all four core papers share Natural Questions test Exact Match.

core_comparison.split: standard test split (minor 3610/3611 preprocessing-version discrepancy is documented)
core_comparison.metric: Exact Match (normalized answer-level EM; higher is better)
comparability_caveats: All rows use Natural Questions open-domain test and answer Exact Match.
REALM uses roughly 13M blocks up to 288 wordpieces and top-5 retrieval; DPR/RAG/FiD generally use the December 2018 Wikipedia corpus split into roughly 21M non-overlapping 100-word passages.
REALM and DPR are extractive readers, whereas RAG and FiD are generative.
The retrieval budget and model capacity change across rows, so the trend is descriptive rather than a controlled ablation.

realm.title: REALM: Retrieval-Augmented Language Model Pre-Training
realm.method_summary: Jointly pre-trains a neural retriever and a masked-language-model knowledge augmenter over an external corpus, then fine-tunes the model for open-domain QA.
realm.retriever: BERT-style dense query/document encoders with maximum inner-product search over Wikipedia blocks
realm.generator_or_reader: BERT-style extractive QA reader / knowledge-augmented encoder
limitations: Index refresh and large-corpus pre-training are computationally expensive and hard to reproduce on student hardware.
The retriever, corpus snapshot, block size, and top-5 budget differ from later systems, so score gains are not a controlled architecture-only comparison.
The retrieved evidence is not presented as a user-facing citation trail.
future_work: Use larger and more diverse external memories while updating them efficiently.
Improve latent retrieval supervision and joint optimization stability.

dpr.title: Dense Passage Retrieval for Open-Domain Question Answering
dpr.method_summary: Trains separate BERT question and passage encoders with in-batch and BM25 hard negatives, indexes 21M passage vectors in FAISS, and feeds retrieved passages to an extractive reader.
dpr.retriever: Two BERT-base encoders, 768-dimensional dot-product vectors, FAISS HNSW
limitations: Retrieval Hit@K only checks whether an answer string occurs in a passage; accidental mentions can count as relevant.
Encoding and indexing about 21 million 768-dimensional passages needs substantial GPU time, RAM, and storage.
The extractive reader cannot freely synthesize evidence across multiple passages, and the corpus is fixed to Wikipedia 2018.
future_work: Improve joint retriever-reader training and reduce the cost of index construction.
Combine dense semantic retrieval with sparse lexical signals for rare exact phrases.

rag.title: Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Knowledge-Intensive NLP Tasks
rag.method_summary: Combines a DPR retriever with a BART generator and marginalizes over retrieved documents either once per output sequence (RAG-Sequence) or at every output token (RAG-Token).
rag.retriever: DPR question encoder over a fixed Wikipedia passage index
limitations: The passage encoder and Wikipedia index are fixed during downstream training, limiting full end-to-end adaptation.
Generation and marginalization over documents add inference cost, while the paper does not provide user-facing evidence citations.
A static Wikipedia snapshot can become stale and retrieval errors can still propagate into generation.
future_work: Jointly update the document encoder and index during task learning.
Apply retrieval-augmented generation to broader tasks and make provenance more explicit.

fid.title: Leveraging Passage Retrieval with Generative Models for Open Domain Question Answering
fid.method_summary: Encodes each question-passage pair independently with T5, concatenates all encoder states, and lets one decoder fuse evidence from as many as 100 passages.
fid.retriever: DPR for Natural Questions/TriviaQA and BM25 for SQuAD Open
limitations: Training with 100 passages is still heavy (the paper used 64 V100 GPUs), even though passage encoding scales linearly.
The retriever is not trained end-to-end with the generator and the passage encodings interact only in the decoder.
Evaluation focuses on short Wikipedia QA and Exact Match rather than explanation quality, provenance, or long-form factuality.
future_work: Train retrieval jointly with the generative reader.
Improve computational efficiency as retrieval depth grows.

shared_research_gaps: A lightweight way to update dense indexes when the corpus changes, without repeating full-corpus embedding.
A calibrated decision rule for when retrieval is necessary and when retrieved evidence is insufficient.
Faithful, page-level provenance: answer quality metrics such as EM do not prove that the generated explanation is supported.
Controlled comparisons that keep generator size, corpus snapshot, chunking, and top-k retrieval budget fixed.
Better handling of tables, formulas, multi-column PDF text, and cross-page evidence during real document ingestion.

supplementary_self_rag.status: kept as supplementary reading, not one of the four numeric core papers
supplementary_self_rag.reason: Self-RAG evaluates TriviaQA with answer-containment accuracy, whereas FiD uses normalized strict Exact Match; 69.3 and 67.6 are therefore not directly comparable.
supplementary_self_rag.use_in_video: Mention briefly as a later idea for adaptive retrieval and self-critique, and explain why it was excluded from the common-metric table.
